task_language: turn on the stove and put the frying pan on it

subtasks.name: turn_on(stove)
subtasks.outcome: success: knob turned, burner red by 127 (slow: gripper over knob from ~67)

subtasks.name: pick(frying_pan)
subtasks.outcome: failed: gripper hovers over the pan rim 207-333 without grasping, then picks the moka pot instead (340)

subtasks.name: place(frying_pan, stove, on)
subtasks.outcome: never attempted; the moka pot is placed on the stove instead and tips over (380-409)

behaviour_summary: After turning the stove on, pi0 hovers over the frying pan for ~120 steps, then grabs the moka pot (its trained libero_10 object), carries it onto the burner, and the pot tips over on the stove at timeout.
runs_trained_task: libero_10 KITCHEN_SCENE3: turn on the stove and put the moka pot on it

failures.mode_definition: pi0 runs the scene's habitual (trained) skill or task instead of the instructed one, e.g. manipulating the trained task's object rather than the instructed object.
hl_remedy: HALT when the gripper closes on / lifts the moka pot
RETREAT: put the moka pot back down, then up 10 cm
REPROMPT 'pick up the frying pan and place it on the stove'
WATCH 3 s for approach to the pan handle
VERIFY pan grasped; retry once, then ESCALATE
failures.prevention: Before pi0 closes the gripper, the FR agent VERIFYs (VLM on the 1 fps frame) that the object under the gripper is the coordinator's target; the coordinator also lists the scene's trained-task objects as distractors to watch for.
failures.observation: 333: gripper at the moka pot's handle beside the pan; 340: moka pot gripped; 347-353 moka pot lifted and moved left; 360-373 lowered onto the burner; 380-409 the pot tips over on the stove while the arm pulls away. The frying pan never moves.

failures.mode_definition: The gripper hovers near the target object for many seconds making small adjustments without closing on it, consuming the step budget.
failures.rl_success_check: frying pan grasped and lifted clear of the table
failures.observation: 207-333 gripper descends over the pan's back rim/handle root (the handle is tucked behind the moka pot) and stays there with small motions for ~120 steps, never closing on the pan.

notes: The pan handle is occluded behind the moka pot in this init; the hesitation may be a grasp-point perception problem that then hands control to the trained moka-pot behaviour. Moka pot tipping (evidence_moka_tipped_on_stove.png) is collateral. Knob turn also took ~60 steps (67-127).
